checks.finding: The two amended facts are each stated determinately enough that two implementers would not build different behaviour. Write-set-size scoping is stated identically at requirements.md:317-355 (REQ-001 step (m): the one-member Block write set is a single temp file + fsync + rename, no staging area, no journal), requirements.md:584-599 (REQ-004: alongside a track's output set it travels through the journaled transaction; as the only artifact written it is direct), requirements.md:1203-1210 (Security Boundaries: the staged-artifact rule does not have the direct write as its subject) and requirements.md:1048-1053 (Main Workflows 4: 'written directly (no staging area ever exists in this branch)'). The per-target live-state obligation is stated once and unambiguously in my inputs, at acceptance-tests.md:93 (TEST-047), and requirements.md's AC-047 (:893) correctly makes no live-state claim, so there is no divergent sibling of it inside the two frozen documents. Three Minor, non-blocking clarifications are recorded and deliberately not failed under the calibration's Finding Evidence Gate item 2, since no implementer decision turns on them: (1) requirements.md:976-988 Roles and Permissions still describes Resolver Evidence instances as written 'via the guarded journaled publication transaction REQ-001 fixes (staged generation, journaled transactional commit...)', a seventh sibling site of the write-set-size fact the remediation did not reach, though its operative subject is authorship (never a human-copy content-population step) rather than mechanism, and the three explicit, dated, ruling-cited sites above govern; (2) requirements.md:1206 justifies the carve-out with 'a Block whose whole write set is Resolver Evidence stages nothing', which is true only in the on-disk .resolver-staging/ sense of 'stage' and false in REQ-001's own in-memory sense, where steps (c)/(i)/(j) have already staged artifacts before any Block at (k)/(l)/(m); (3) requirements.md:385 calls a hypothetical additional diagnostic id 'a nineteenth diagnostic-id value of its own' while the enum is closed at sixteen at requirements.md:361-386, AC-010, AC-014, REQ-004 and acceptance-tests.md TEST-010/TEST-014 - a stale ordinal, not a behavioural fork.

The publication-journal-recovery unconvergeable branch is required to leave a live state that two other frozen statements declare can never persist. Evidence: (a) acceptance-tests.md:93 (TEST-047, amended this round) requires the companion fixture to assert that 'every interrupted target other than resolver-evidence.yaml is byte-identical to its pre-invocation state - the recovery algorithm attempts no partial rollback and no repair once it declares the journal unconvergeable'; (b) requirements.md:372 fixes that pre-invocation state as a crash-interrupted multi-target batch, since the row fires exactly when 'a referenced pre-image backup file is itself missing/unreadable, or a target's current live hash matches neither its journal-recorded PRE nor POST value'; (c) requirements.md:1173-1175 (Edge Cases, crash-between-two-renames bullet) nevertheless states unconditionally that the next invocation 'converges every target back to one of the transaction's own two terminal states - fully-applied or fully-reverted - before proceeding with its own, separate work, never leaving a mixed generation standing'; (d) requirements.md:1210-1218 (Security Boundaries) states that a crash 'at any point, including between two renames', a Block, an in-process publication failure or a post-publication-verification mismatch each leave every live path 'either fully absent, fully unchanged ... never a torn or partially-written artifact, and never a mixed generation across a multi-target batch'. (c) and (d) cannot both hold alongside (a)+(b): the TEST-047 companion fixture instantiates precisely a batch in which one target stands at POST and another at PRE (or at neither), and requires that state to survive the Block untouched. Downstream failure mode: the Phase-2 implementer of REQ-001's mandatory step-(0) recovery scan cannot decide whether an unconvergeable journal obliges a best-effort repair or partial rollback to satisfy (c)/(d), or obliges touching nothing to satisfy (a); a verifier deriving an invariant check from (d) and the author of the TEST-047 fixture would assert mutually exclusive post-conditions on the identical run, so one acceptance obligation fails by construction whichever behaviour is built. This belongs to specification review, not to design, task or quality-gate review: both statements are normative text inside this package's frozen Phase-1 artifacts (requirements.md and acceptance-tests.md), no design or implementation choice can satisfy both, and leaving it open hands the impl-policy gate a frozen-document-versus-frozen-document deadlock of exactly the kind investigation.md:1344-1434 records as the origin of the D(1)/D(2) cycle. Severity Critical: it is a durability/atomicity safety boundary asserted in the Security Boundaries section, and the conflict is direct and behavioural (repair versus no repair) rather than a matter of emphasis. Two aggravating same-class details: requirements.md:1219-1226, the very next Security Boundaries bullet, does carry the correct exception ('always resolved (or, if unrecoverable, fails this invocation closed with publication-journal-recovery)'), which shows the absolutes at (c)/(d) are unmaintained siblings rather than a deliberate stance; and the clause in (d) permitting a fully-written path '(Resolver Evidence only, on a Block reached before publication)' does not cover the step-(m) Blocks artifact-publication-failed and post-publication-generation-mismatch, for which requirements.md:333-338 and REQ-004:584-599 both require Evidence to be written and AC-012 (:858) grants no exception. Both sentences sit in the bullet commit e6884a39 edited as site 3 of six, so the remediation landed in that bullet's first sentence and left its second sentence, and its Edge Cases sibling, stating the pre-amendment rule - the propagation-drift defect investigation.md:1517-1522 names as this package's recurring one.

All sixteen Block diagnostics are enumerated and fixtured one-for-one (acceptance-tests.md:59 TEST-010, cross-checked against requirements.md:371-386 - I counted sixteen table rows and the fixture list names the same sixteen ids). Empty state: zero affected components is covered as a legitimate non-Block resolution at requirements.md:1073-1092 and locked by a separate fixture at TEST-018 (:67), with the [] trigger_evaluations cardinality argument stated explicitly. Boundary/race states: TEST-040 (:86) pre-publication TOCTOU including the ownership_digest-identical-but-affected_components-differ case, TEST-048 (:94), TEST-049 (:95) post-publication race with journal rollback, TEST-047 (:93) crash recovery in both its converging and unconvergeable branches, TEST-057 (:103) the step-(e) detection recheck, TEST-058 (:104) the absent-component fail-closed path. Negative paths: TEST-011 (:60) no-partial-artifact over every Block fixture, TEST-038 (:84) staged-but-never-published, TEST-039 (:85) injected write/rename failure with journal-based rollback rather than a bare unlink, TEST-055 (:101) both sub-cases of output-schema-validation-failed including the self-referential write-nothing case, TEST-056 (:102) warn/block cardinality including the abort exception, TEST-013 (:62) all three exit codes. The one uncovered logical state, required-present-empty, is disclosed with its reason at acceptance-tests.md:58 (Epic A2's lite_policy schema admits no such key today, so a fixture would not itself pass validate-capability-registry) rather than silently omitted, which is an honest, argued gap and not a missing negative path. The CONTRADICTION finding above concerns what TEST-047 asserts, not whether the edge case is covered.

Every assumption is either resolved by investigation or carries an explicit pre-design/pre-implementation decision owner. requirements.md:1246-1269 lists three assumptions, each with a named resolution path: the four sibling contracts landing unmodified from their Passed state (with a follow-up-edit obligation if any changes materially), the protected-suffix reservation being live in guard-invariants.json (with an explicit re-verify-then-choose-sequencing fallback), and the SKILL.md unprotected status being a re-verified snapshot rather than a guarantee. Open Questions (:1271-1291) are each dispositioned: OQ-001 and OQ-002 are deferred to a named future caller/epic and are consistent with the Non-goals at :794-796, and OQ-003 is recorded as resolved by INV-020 with a concrete file:line anchor plus the AC-053 fingerprint mechanism. The one cross-epic gap that could otherwise be invented downstream - no Registry field to source required_lite_checks from - is named with an owner, a scope, a migration note and a blocked-consumer boundary at requirements.md:137-163 and again as a Risk at :1295-1325, and investigation.md INV-019 (:515) is its evidence. The amendment history itself is resolvable rather than assumed: investigation.md:1344-1567 records rulings D(1)/D(2) including the withdrawn half, with full commit hashes fa1ad0e0/c6f6242b/c44d056d/e6884a39, verbatim dated approvals, and per-document SHA-256 values at e6884a39 (:1560-1566) that match my manifest's requirements.md and acceptance-tests.md digests exactly.

The human-approval and irreversible-change boundaries this package implies are stated and testable. Human approval: requirements.md:965-975 fixes that the three Resolver scripts' code content is staged under specs/<feature>/human-copy/ for human application via apply-human-copy and is never a direct agent write to the protected live path, scoped explicitly to immutable code only; acceptance-tests.md:75 (TEST-026) makes that observable by requiring a staged candidate with a correct MANIFEST.sha256 entry and records the Status as resolving through a human cp action; requirements.md:989-994 assigns the future SKILL.md task an explicit re-verify-protection-status decision, and the Assumptions at :1255-1264 give the fallback if the reservation is not yet live. Scope boundary: AC-032/TEST-032 (requirements.md:878, acceptance-tests.md:81) make the plugins/** non-edit boundary checkable by git diff against this package's own commits, matching the Non-goal at :805-810. Irreversible-change boundary: the publication transaction is the only path by which this feature mutates live artifacts, and it is guarded by AC-011 (:857), AC-038 (:884), AC-039 (:885), AC-047 (:893) and AC-049 (:895), each with a fixture. Post-implementation amendment approval is itself durably recorded rather than asserted: investigation.md:1361-1364 and :1405-1419 carry verbatim, dated approval quotations for D(1) and D(2) with the option text as presented, and :1452-1464 gives full commit hashes, satisfying the calibration's Amendment Re-Review Context evidence bar; I therefore raised no phase-sequencing finding, and none of my findings rests on phase-sequencing.

No product behaviour is missing that an implementation-policy reviewer would have to invent. The CLI surface including which flags are required and which default is fixed at requirements.md:231-248 with AC-001/TEST-001; the processing order is fixed step-by-step at :249-355 with each Block site named; the refusal taxonomy is a closed sixteen-row machine-readable table at :371-386 with an exit-code contract at AC-013; the new artifact's schema fields, cardinality bindings, bidirectional-consistency rules and declaration_index keying are fixed at :474-621; the caller integration contract has a concrete file:line insertion anchor plus a position-sensitive fingerprint at :720-754 and AC-053; Roles and Permissions (:963-994), Security Boundaries (:1178-1242) and Non-goals (:766-818) each draw the ownership and scope lines a design reviewer would otherwise have to guess. Every acceptance criterion has a matching test row except the three Global rows the preamble documents as its one exception class, and the AC-057/AC-058 propagation gap this round closed means the declared 1:1 mapping now holds in both directions (58 criteria, 55 test rows). One caveat, charged under CONTRADICTION above rather than counted twice here: readiness is conditional on the unconvergeable-journal conflict being closed in Phase 1, because it is a conflict between frozen statements rather than an omission, and an impl-policy reviewer cannot resolve it without re-opening these two documents.
